document_summary: WBUR news article (June 23, 2026) reporting that the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court struck from the November 2026 ballot a statewide rent control initiative because it included a religious-use exemption.

rules.title: 2026 statewide rent control ballot question (struck by SJC)
rules.requirement: The proposed ballot initiative would have limited annual rent increases for residences in Massachusetts, but the Supreme Judicial Court ruled it cannot go on the November 2026 ballot because its religious-use exemption makes it a measure relating to religion, which the state Constitution bars from the initiative process.
rules.key_value: Would have capped annual rent increases statewide; struck from ballot, so no rent cap enacted
rules.coverage_conditions: Proposed to cover residences statewide, with exemptions for several unit types.
rules.exemptions: Proposed exemptions included units "operated solely for … religious … purposes" and other secular unit types.
rules.interaction: Because the measure failed, no statewide rent control exists in Massachusetts; supporters hinted at a possible 2028 ballot petition and a legislative compromise was not passed before July 1.
rules.citation: Mass. Const. amend. art. 48, The Initiative, Pt. II, § 2 (SJC ruling, June 2026)
rules.quoted_span: The state’s Supreme Judicial Court ruled a ballot question seeking to bring rent control back to Massachusetts cannot go forward this November, because it includes a religious exemption.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary news source; the case name and the SJC's exact citation are not given in the article. The measure was never enacted, so effective_date is null. Article is dated June 23, 2026 (updated and originally published). Existing Massachusetts law is not addressed in this article.
